name: Alliant Energy
key_signal: LNT trades near 52-week highs and above both moving averages (golden cross intact) but momentum is stalling—MACD histogram just turned negative and the stock fell 1.2% while trailing P/E sits at a rich 23.5x for a low-growth regulated utility.
thesis: Alliant remains a textbook defensive utility trade: beta of 0.54, above both the 50- and 200-day moving averages, a golden cross signal, and 126-day momentum of +13.7% show the uptrend is well established and consensus is a 'buy' across 13 covering analysts. Revenue growth (5%) and earnings growth (4.9%) are modest but steady, margins are healthy (21% operating margin), and the 2.86% dividend yield offers income support in a market where rate-sensitive utilities have been rerating higher as rate-cut expectations solidify. Being a large, well-covered S&P 500 name with low volatility (20.7% annualized) makes it a reasonable rotation destination if risk appetite fades.
bear_case: The stock is priced for perfection at 23.5x trailing and 20.3x forward earnings with a 2.6x price-to-book against an ROE of just 11.3%, leaving little room for multiple expansion in a sector growing revenue at only 5%. Debt-to-equity of ~160% combined with deeply negative free cash flow (-$1.2B) signals the company is funding heavy capex/rate-base growth with debt issuance, a vulnerability if long-term yields back up and utility valuations compress; the recent negative MACD histogram and stalling RSI (48.5, right at neutral) after a ~13.7% six-month run suggest the easy momentum gains are behind it, and the stock is already 5% below its 52-week high with a down day and negative daily return signaling possible near-term consolidation or pullback toward the 50-day SMA at $73.78.
